41#main: 297—The laws of crossbreeding and the conduct of kilay beheimah. In it are 16 seifim. (297—1) One who mates a male with a female that is not its species—whether in livestock, whether in wild animals and birds, and even in sea animal species—behold he receives lashes.
42#main: (297—2) He does not receive lashes until he inserts with his hand like a tube in a reed. But if he brought them one upon another alone, or aroused them with voice—they give him lashes of rebellion.
43#main: (297—3) It is permitted to bring two species into one pen; and if he saw them mating one with another, he is not obligated to separate them. {Rama: And in a place where there is reason to fear licentiousness that they will do a prohibition, it is forbidden to bring them in even to a pen (Nimukei Yosef on the chapter HaSho'el).}
44#main: (297—4) It is forbidden for an Israelite to give his animal to a non-Jew for mating. {Rama: And likewise any statement to a non-Jew—even for a negative commandment—is forbidden (there). Unless the non-Jew does it for his own benefit (Hagahot Mordechai on Shabbat).}
45#main: (297—5) One who transgressed and mated his animal as kilayim—behold what is born from them is permitted in benefit; and if it was a pure species with a pure species, it is permitted in eating.
46#main: (297—6) Every two species of livestock or wild animal—even though they resemble one another and grow one with another and conceive one from another—since they are two species, they are forbidden because of kilayim. How so? Wolf with dog, village dog (meaning: a dog raised in villages—it is small and resembles a fox) with fox, goats with gazelles, ibexes with sheep, horse with mule, mule with donkey, donkey with wild ass (meaning: a wild donkey growing in the desert)—kilayim one with another.
47#main: (297—7) A species that has wild and domesticated, such as wild ox with ox, and remakh (meaning: a horse from the sons of the Remachim) with horse—they are permitted one with another. But domestic goose with wild goose are kilayim one with another, because the domestic goose lays its eggs inside and the wild goose lays its eggs outside—from which it is clear they are two species.
48#main: (297—8) The koy is kilayim with wild animal and with livestock, and one does not receive lashes on it because it is a doubt.
49#main: (297—9) Those born from kilayim—if their mothers were one species, it is permitted to mate them one with another; and if their mothers were two species, it is forbidden to mate them one with another, even though their fathers were another species. And it is forbidden to mate this offspring even on its mother's species. How so? A mule whose mother was a donkey—it is permitted to mate it on a mule whose mother was a donkey; and it is forbidden to mate it even on a donkey. But a mule whose mother was a horse—it is forbidden to mate it on a mule whose mother was a donkey, and likewise all similar cases. Therefore one who wishes to mate a mule on a mule or to drive with two mules examines the signs of ears and tail and voice—if they resemble one another, it is known their mothers were one species and they are permitted.
50#main: (297—10) It is forbidden to do work with two species, such as to plow and to pull with a wagon and the like—whether one is impure and one pure, whether both impure, whether both pure; whether livestock with livestock such as pig with sheep, or wild with wild such as ibex with elephant, or wild with livestock such as dog with goat, or deer with pig, and the like.
51#main: (297—11) Whether one plows, sows, pulls them with a wagon or stone as one, or drives them as one—even with voice he receives lashes. {Rama: A non-Jew driving kilayim—it is permitted for an Israelite to greet him or speak with him in a loud voice, for we are not concerned lest the animals go because of his voice—for in all prohibitions an unintended act is permitted if it is not a definite outcome (pesik reisha). But if an Israelite walks on the road with a non-Jew and an Israelite's load is on the non-Jew's wagon that he drives as kilayim, the Israelite may not walk near the wagon, for sometimes the wagon is pressed and he will shout at the animals to go quickly—and this is forbidden because of driving kilayim (Terumat HaDeshen siman 298).} But the one who harnesses is exempt until he pulls or until he drives. {Rama: And some say it is forbidden to drive them or pull them only when tied together (Tur in the name of the Rosh); therefore it is permitted for a rider to pull with a rope a dog beside a horse (there in the name of Avi HaEzri). And some disagree (there in the name of R' Efraim).}
52#main: (297—12) A wagon that they were pulling as kilayim—it is forbidden to sit in it even though he did not drive, because his sitting causes them to pull the wagon. And likewise it is forbidden for one to sit in the wagon and one to drive.
53#main: (297—13) Even a hundred who drove as one receive lashes.
54#main: (297—14) If he tied two horses to one wagon, it is forbidden to tie a donkey with them even though the two horses can pull it without the donkey.
55#main: (297—15) A wagon pulling with a wagon of one species—he does not tie one species with a rope neither at the side of the wagon nor behind the wagon. {Rama: Because it pushes the wagon in its walking (Tur).}
56#main: (297—16) It is permitted to do work with a person and livestock or wild animal as one, such as a person plowing with an ox, or pulling a wagon with a donkey, and the like.
